response.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT ma.major_id, ma.department, COUNT(*) AS member_count FROM member m JOIN major ma ON m.link_to_major = ma.major_id GROUP BY ma.major_id, ma.department), shares AS (SELECT major_id, department, member_count, CAST(member_count AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(member_count) FROM counts) AS share FROM counts), dept AS (SELECT *, AVG(share) OVER (PARTITION BY department) AS dept_avg FROM shares) SELECT major_id, department, member_count, share, share - dept_avg AS diff_above_avg FROM dept WHERE share > dept_avg ORDER BY diff_above_avg DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Department averages are taken over only majors that have at least one matching member (majors with zero members do not appear in the count and so are not included in the average).
Total members with a matching major equals the sum of per-major counts (inner join on major_id).

alternatives.interpretation: Include majors with zero members when averaging shares within each department (their share is 0).
